notes:
A response with no words in it is no longer judged as the page.

Some servers answer an automated client with a short stand-in instead of the
page — a rate limiter, an edge rule, a bot filter. One classifieds site returned
24 URLs as 641 bytes of markup with no title and not one word, under a
non-standard HTTP status that still counts as success.

Docket judged that stand-in as the site's own content: nine findings named those
URLs, 214 page-claims, three of them HIGH — no content, no title tag, no mobile
viewport. Every one was false; the pages serve full content in a browser.

Those responses are now recognised and taken out of the judged set, and reported
separately so you can see Docket was not shown them. A genuinely empty page is
still reported as an empty page.
